themes_detail.label: Elevator Failures Surge
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints spiked to 5 THIS WEEK vs. a baseline of 0.5 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 900% increase (z-score: 9.0)—suggesting a sudden cluster of mechanical failures or maintenance gaps affecting residential and commercial buildings in South Beach/Dongan Hills.
evidence: 5 elevator complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average over 8 weeks (900% spike)
Z-score of 9.0 indicates statistically extreme outlier event
Affects mobility and safety in a district with aging residential stock (evident from 346 alteration permits filed in 90 days)
reporting_angles: Interview residents in affected buildings about wait times, safety concerns, and impact on elderly and disabled residents
File DOB records requests to determine which buildings are generating complaints and whether they have violation histories

themes_detail.label: Sanitation Crisis Emerging
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary condition complaints jumped to 12 THIS WEEK vs. a 5.2-per-week average over 8 weeks—a 129% increase (z-score: 6.19)—indicating a sharp deterioration in street and property cleanliness across the district.
evidence: 12 unsanitary condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.2 weekly average (129% spike)
Z-score of 6.19 confirms statistically significant anomaly
Community Board has made repeated 'other expense request' for DSNY—suggesting sanitation has been a chronic pain point
reporting_angles: Geo-map the 12 complaints to identify whether a single neighborhood block or multiple areas are affected
Contact DSNY to ask whether staffing, collection routes, or street conditions changed this week

themes_detail.label: Building Maintenance Failures
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance or facility complaints surged to 10 THIS WEEK vs. a 2.2-per-week baseline over 8 weeks—a 344% increase (z-score: 6.46)—pointing to widespread building system breakdowns across residential and public facilities.
evidence: 10 maintenance/facility complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.2 weekly average (344% spike)
Z-score of 6.46 indicates highly abnormal spike
Correlates with elevator spike (5 complaints this week)—suggests systemic building infrastructure strain
reporting_angles: Determine whether elevator complaints and maintenance complaints are from the same buildings or separate incidents
Interview property managers or building owners about whether cold weather, age of stock, or staffing shortages are driving failures

themes_detail.label: Missing Street Signs Spike
themes_detail.summary: Street sign complaints jumped to 6 TWO WEEKS AGO vs. a 0.8-per-week average—a 700% spike (z-score: 6.33)—indicating either traffic accidents, seasonal weather damage, or theft affecting wayfinding and public safety.
evidence: 6 missing street sign complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.8 weekly average (700% spike)
Z-score of 6.33 confirms extreme statistical anomaly
Community Board requests DOT funding for 'other expense'—suggests transportation infrastructure has chronic issues
reporting_angles: Walk the district to visually audit which intersections are missing signs and assess traffic safety risk
Contact DOT about timeline for sign replacement and whether this correlates with weather events or construction

themes_detail.label: Bus Stop Infrastructure Failures
themes_detail.summary: Bus stop shelter placement complaints spiked to 3 LAST WEEK vs. a 0.1-per-week baseline—a 2300% increase (z-score: 8.69)—suggesting either new transit stops being added without proper amenities or existing shelters failing.
evidence: 3 bus stop shelter complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (2300% spike)
Z-score of 8.69 indicates highly abnormal event
Affects transit-dependent residents in a district with ongoing transit infrastructure renewal
reporting_angles: Identify which 3 bus stops generated complaints and what specific shelter issues were reported (missing, damaged, unsafe placement)
Contact MTA/NYC DOT to determine if new routes or shelter installations are underway in South Beach/Dongan Hills
